title: Bram and the Lantern
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, courier Casper Okonkwo carries sealed dispatches through a country sliding into civil war, guided by a promise made years earlier to a lantern-keeper's daughter in the border town of Halven. When one dispatch names that same family as traitors to be silenced by the republic's own agents, Casper must choose between his oath of delivery and the people who once gave him shelter. Pursued by his former handler, Captain Ilsa Rehn, and shadowed by the boy courier he was meant to train, he races to expose the forged evidence before the family is executed. The book ends with Casper burning the true orders and delivering instead a letter of exoneration — saving the family but exiling himself forever from the nation he served.
about_author: Casper Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states, an experience that taught him how much history turns on what fits inside an envelope. Bram and the Lantern is their second novel, following a well-received debut about railway telegraph operators during a border war.

chapters.title: What Fits in a Saddlebag
chapters.summary: Casper Okonkwo, POV. In the capital of Vessany, Casper receives his final assignment: three sealed dispatches to be carried north as the republic collapses. He measures his life in portable things — codes, coins, a brass lantern charm. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: The Promise at Halven
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Casper's POV. Seven years earlier, wounded and stranded, Casper was hidden for a winter by the Veren family — lantern-makers — and swore to return with news when peace came. Emotional beat: warmth and debt, the origin of his loyalty.

chapters.title: Orders Are Orders
chapters.summary: Casper's POV on the road north. He meets his young shadow, apprentice courier Tam, assigned without explanation. The first dispatch resists all attempts at casual inspection; its weight feels wrong. Emotional beat: unease hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: A Town That Buries Its Bells
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The pair pass through a village stripped of anything worth looting; Tam reveals fragments of why he was really assigned — to watch Casper. Emotional beat: wary companionship, two liars sharing a fire.

chapters.title: The Seal That Shouldn't Open
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. At a relay station, Casper discovers the second dispatch bears a forgery — the chancery seal is a month old, but the paper is older. Someone has pre-written history. Emotional beat: the first crack in his faith.

chapters.title: Captain Rehn
chapters.summary: Ilsa Rehn's POV. His former handler follows the same road, carrying verbal orders: the couriers are expendable once delivery is confirmed. Rehn respects Casper and intends to kill him anyway. Emotional beat: cold duty, almost affectionate menace.

chapters.title: Lantern Smoke
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He reaches Halven and finds the town under occupation; the Veren workshop is boarded, and soldiers are asking questions about 'the family that helped spies.' Emotional beat: homecoming turned to ash.

chapters.title: The Daughter in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Mira Veren's POV. Hidden beneath the ruined workshop, Mira tends her injured father and waits for the promised courier she half-believed was a story. Casper finds her by the old signal — three taps, lantern light. Emotional beat: relief edged with grief.

chapters.title: Reading Another Man's Mail
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Against every oath, he opens the second dispatch: it orders the arrest and execution of the Veren family on fabricated charges of treason, dated before the alleged crime. Emotional beat: horror, and the death of his innocence about the republic.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam catches Casper with the open dispatch and must decide whether to report him. He burns the incriminating wrapper instead, confessing he was sent to watch a man he'd come to admire. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into allegiance.

chapters.title: The Road Back Is Longer
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The trio flees south toward the provisional assembly where the exoneration could still be filed — carrying the third, unopened dispatch as their only leverage. Rehn picks up their trail. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: River Crossing at Dusk
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. A ferryman demands payment they don't have; Mira trades her father's finest lantern, the symbol of everything her family built. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the cost of belonging to something worth saving.

chapters.title: What Rehn Carries
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Closing in, Rehn reflects on her decades of service to a state that no longer exists, and admits privately she suspects the charges are forged — and will deliver them regardless. Emotional beat: tragic integrity, loyalty as a cage.

chapters.title: The Third Dispatch
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Cornered at a chapel, Casper finally opens the last dispatch: it is his own death warrant, signed in advance, proof the mission was always meant to end with him silenced. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallized into clarity.

chapters.title: Three Taps on Glass
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam volunteers as decoy, using the courier signals Casper taught him to lead Rehn's men astray through the marshes. He is captured. Emotional beat: the student outgrowing the teacher, at terrible price.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lantern Light
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Rehn interrogates Tam and recognizes in him the courier she once was. Tam offers her the opened death warrant as evidence. She pockets it without committing either way. Emotional beat: doubt planted in stone.

chapters.title: The Assembly of Ashes
chapters.summary: Casper and Mira's POV alternating. They reach the provisional assembly, only to find it dissolved; the clerk who could file exoneration is packing to flee. Casper bargains with the one thing left: the original forged dispatch itself. Emotional beat: hope running on fumes.

chapters.title: Rehn's Decision
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Ordered to execute Casper on sight, Rehn arrives at the assembly, reads the forged charges against the death warrant bearing Casper's name, and understands the machine she served would have burned them all. Emotional beat: the breaking of a lifelong loyalty.

chapters.title: The Burning of the True Orders
chapters.summary: Climax, Casper's POV. Confronted by Rehn's soldiers, Casper publicly burns the execution orders and delivers instead the exoneration letter, staking his life on the truth. Rehn stands down her men, arresting her own lieutenant instead. Emotional beat: the promise kept at maximum cost.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The Veren name is cleared, but the republic is finished; Mira's father dies peacefully knowing it. Mira asks Casper what he carries now. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude, found family made explicit.

chapters.title: Exile's Inventory
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Stripped of rank and citizenship, Casper inventories his life again: a codebook he'll never use, a lantern charm returned, a new letter of introduction written by the family he saved. Emotional beat: loss transformed into freedom.

chapters.title: Bram and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Tam's POV. Years later, Tam — now a courier for the new border towns — visits Casper and Mira, married and running a rebuilt workshop in neutral territory. A lantern hangs in the window, always lit, the old signal meaning safe harbor. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.
